blocks.content: A Money Bill shall not be introduced in a Legislative Council, and the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the State.

rows: Exclusive right to introduce and pass Money Bills

stats.value: Max Total Delay on Ordinary Bills

items: There is NO provision for a joint sitting of the two houses at the state level to resolve a legislative deadlock.
The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly has the final authority to decide whether a bill is a Money Bill.
Only elected members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs) participate in the election of the President of India and members of the Rajya Sabha.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Money Bills can originate only in the Legislative Assembly and cannot be rejected or substantially altered by the Legislative Council.
The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible exclusively to the Legislative Assembly, which holds the sole power to pass a No-Confidence Motion.
The Legislative Assembly possesses the exclusive power to vote on Demands for Grants presented in the state budget.
Under Article 169, the Assembly can pass a resolution by a special majority to create or abolish the state Legislative Council.
Unlike Parliament, there is no provision for a joint sitting in state legislatures; the ultimate authority on ordinary legislation rests with the Legislative Assembly.
